installMethods.publisherPin: Claude Code plugin 'unslop' from the marketplace heydamir/unslop (publisher-stated; not checked against the marketplace)
Codex and Antigravity: the host installs or the user copies the skill folder into a skills folder (publisher-stated; not run, no path used)

dependencies: Node.js to run the skill's .mjs scripts; no version is stated in the files read
Playwright with a Chromium browser, only for page snapshots and story videos (publisher-stated)
ffmpeg on the PATH, only for story videos (publisher-stated)
An image service connected to the host, only for optional generated visuals (publisher-stated)
privilegeClaims: The skill edits the project's front-end source files when the user asks; the publisher says it audits and proposes a direction first (README, SKILL.md)
SKILL.md tells the agent to render the screen and take screenshots, and to run node scripts from the skill folder
snapshot.mjs launches Chromium through Playwright and writes an HTML copy and a PNG into a folder the caller names (read, not run)
story.mjs starts a local web server on 127.0.0.1, launches Chromium, runs ffmpeg and writes frame files then an MP4 (read, not run)
The README installs the Claude Code plugin for all projects by default; project-only scopes exist (publisher-stated)
plugin.json and marketplace.json declare no hooks, MCP server or command (those two files read, not the whole tree)
networkClaims: snapshot.mjs loads a given URL and fetches its style sheets, images and fonts, then stores them inline in one local HTML file (read, not run)
The skill can use an image service such as fal, Replicate, OpenAI images or Higgsfield, or offer to connect one as an MCP server; it says it asks before each paid generation (publisher-stated)
Installing Playwright, Chromium and ffmpeg is a separate publisher step that downloads software; this app does none of it
The files read contain no telemetry statement either way, so telemetry is recorded as unknown
The README advertises a paid design service by the author; the skill itself is free under CC BY 4.0 (publisher-stated)

notes: The host agent reads and may edit the project's source files and screens it works on; that content is processed by the host's model provider under the host's own account and terms. What leaves the machine depends on the host, the browser and any image service, not on this record.

A generated visual may send a prompt that describes the user's product to a third-party image service, and some services are paid. The publisher says the prompt is shown and approval is asked first; that was read, not tested.
Saving a live site copies that site's page content and assets into the project folder; the site's own terms apply to that content.
